    12  /-!
    13  # Dilatransvections generate the special linear group
    14  
    15  We prove the theorem of [dieudonne-1955][J. Dieudonné, “Sur les générateurs
    16  des groupes classiques”].
    17  
    18  Let `K` be a division ring and `V` be a `K`-module.
    19  
    20  * `LinearEquiv.mem_transvections_pow_mul_dilatransvections_of_fixedReduce_eq_one`:
    21    If `e.fixedReduce = 1`, then `e` can be written as the product
    22    of `finrank K (V ⧸ e.fixedSubmodule) - 1` transvections
    23    and one dilatransvection.
    24    This is the first part of the non-exceptional case in Dieudonné's theorem.
    25    (This statement is not interesting when `e = 1`.)
    26  
    27  * `LinearEquiv.mem_transvections_pow_mul_dilatransvections_of_fixedReduce_ne_smul_id`:
    28    If `e.fixedReduce` is not a homothety, then `e` can be written as the product
    29    of `finrank K (V ⧸ e.fixedSubmodule) - 1` transvections and one dilatransvection.
    30    This is the second part of the non-exceptional case in Dieudonné's theorem.
    31  
    32  * `LinearEquiv.IsExceptional`:
    33    A linear equivalence `e : V ≃ₗ[K] V` is exceptional if `1 < finrank K (V ⧸ e.fixedSubmodule)`
    34    and if `e.fixedReduce` is a nontrivial homothety.
    35  
    36  * `LinearEquiv.mem_dilatransvections_pow_of_not_isExceptional`:
    37    This is the non-exceptional case in Dieudonné's theorem,
    38    as a combination of the two preceding statements.
    39  
    40  ## TODO
    41  
    42  * Prove the third and fourth cases of Dieudonné's theorem that
    43    concern the case where `e` is exceptional:
    44    `e` can be written as the product of `finrank K (V ⧸ e.fixedSubmodule)`
    45    transvections and one dilatransvection but not less.
    46  
    47  * Prove that the general linear group is generated by dilatransvections.
    48  
    49  * Prove that the special linear group is generated by transvections
    50    (with a bound on the minimal number of transvections needed).
    51  
    52  * In the statements above, the dilatransvection is at the right of the product;
    53    show that it can be inserted anywhere.
    54    (The point is that transvections normalize dilatransvections.)
    55
